title: The ASASSN-14ko flare-fluence link to the timing stall depends on the assumed time order
abstract: We test whether the larger flare fluence in the ASASSN-14ko timing stall gives secure evidence for a physical clock-emission link. We use 16 source-published optical flare fits and enumerate joint rank tests of rise width, decline time, fluence and peak amplitude. For the fixed published stall window, the fluence difference survives correction for four properties: the adjusted tail fraction is 0.003871. No single flare drives it. The global tail fraction rises to 0.05357 for adjacent-pair permutations, 0.08333 for four-flare blocks and 0.1875 for cyclic shifts. Without the unusual 2022 flares, the four-property tail fraction is 0.09441. A no-restart grouping, motivated by newer Einstein Probe timing, moves the strongest exchangeable-row evidence from fluence to rise width. The full-sample fluence difference is robust under exchangeability, but its link to orbital evolution depends on assumptions about temporal persistence and the clock regime. The block and cyclic tests are conditional sensitivity tests, not proof that the association is absent. We obtain no new telescope data. Fit errors, missing cycles and uncertainty in timing boundaries are not propagated.

display.caption: Exact joint optical tests and their sensitivity to time order. Cyclic phases refer to observed-flare order, with irregular orbital-cycle gaps.

citations.reason: We test its morphology association with exact joint rank tests and time-order sensitivity.
Its new X-ray timing motivates the no-restart sensitivity analysis.
Its optical-marker clock underlies the source timing regimes.
